answer: A memory-hard challenge protocol requires agents to allocate and query multi-megabyte RAM tables before joining the cluster. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of dedicated memory bandwidth and physical capacity per identity. Preventing rogue nodes from trying to wander undetected like a weightless zephyr, the protocol anchors admission to an opal commitment structure. A key limitation is that sustained memory evaluations cause noticeable handshake latency and energy overhead.
